extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and NIH peer reviewers (study section members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting NIH first-level (study section) peer review of grant applications, including overall impact assessment, scoring, core review criteria, and the simplified 2025+ framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary focus is determining 'the overall impact that your proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field(s) involved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess the likely overall impact on the field(s). The overall impact score is not a mathematical sum or mean of the individual criterion scores; reviewers weigh different criteria as they see fit when forming the overall impact judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical rating scale used for scored elements of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 1-9 numerical rating (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor). Calculation: Final Overall Impact score = (mean of all panelist scores) × 10. Result Range: 10 (high impact) to 90 (low impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the problem; will the project drive change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the five core review criteria (legacy). Consider whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field and whether successful completion would have meaningful impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the qualifications, experience, productivity, and complementary expertise of the principal investigator(s) and collaborators relative to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it shift current paradigms or use novel methods?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project challenges existing paradigms, employs novel concepts, approaches or methodologies, or advances technical capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the strategy, methodology, analyses well-reasoned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the overall strategy, study design, methodology, and analyses for rigor, appropriateness, feasibility, and consideration of potential problems and alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the scientific environment, institutional support, equipment, and other resources will contribute to the likelihood of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the Research (Significance + Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2025+ simplified factor combining Significance and Innovation into 'Importance of the Research'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications due on or after January 25, 2025, NIH evaluates Importance of the Research as a single factor encompassing both Significance and Innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications due on or after January 25, 2025, Rigor and Feasibility captures the quality of the Approach (strategy, methodology, analyses) as a primary factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise and Resources (Investigator + Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2025+ simplified factor combining Investigator and Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications due on or after January 25, 2025, Expertise and Resources reflects the combined assessment of the research team and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria that receive individual numerical scores (1-9) that directly contribute to Overall Impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria are individually rated on the 1-9 scale and those scores inform the Overall Impact judgment; they are the direct scored elements of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria that do not receive individual numerical scores but influence Overall Impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include human subjects protection and animal welfare. These considerations should inform the Overall Impact assessment even though they are not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Items that do not affect scoring but address programmatic issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These considerations (e.g., budget justification) do not change the scores but should be noted for program officers and programmatic decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Probability by Overall Impact Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance mapping Overall Impact score ranges to likelihood of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores 10-30: most likely to be funded. Scores 31-45: might be funded. Scores >46: rarely funded. Note that the final funding decision also involves programmatic priorities and budget constraints.
